exposure: pregnancy within 24 months of renal transplantation
pregnancy more than 24 months after renal transplantation
outcome: Proteinuria during the third trimester of pregnancy
cohort: 44 patients who became pregnant following renal transplantation
finding: A longer interval between renal transplantation and pregnancy is associated with better pregnancy outcomes, including longer gestational age, higher birth weight, and lower incidence of preterm labor.
mod_finding: For pregnancies occurring less than or more than 24 months after renal transplantation, normal vaginal delivery occurred in 55% and 58.3% of cases, respectively, and cesarean section was performed in 45% and 41.6% of cases, respectively.
